d_sv_content.name: Clinical Testing of Canine T Cells Engineered to Target Soft Tissue Sarcoma with Oral Immunotherapy
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us test a new combination therapy for soft tissue sarcoma in dogs.
d_sv_content.description:
This study is evaluating a new type of cancer treatment for dogs with soft tissue sarcoma. The treatment uses your dog’s own immune cells (called T cells) to help fight cancer.

A blood sample is collected (about 3-4 tablespoons), and the T cells are modified in a lab to better recognize and attack cancer cells. These upgraded cells (called CAR T cells) are then given back to your dog through an IV infusion.

Dogs in this study may also receive oral immunotherapy medications to help improve how well the treatment works.

The goal of this study is to determine if this treatment is safe and effective in dogs with soft tissue sarcoma.
d_sv_content.requirements: Blood collection to create CAR T cellsTumor biopsy at enrollmentPre-treatment oral chemotherapyOne-day hospital stay for CAR T cell infusionFollow-up visits after infusionSurgery to remove the tumor (or repeat biopsy) about 1 week after treatmentRechecks at 1, 2, and 6 weeks after surgery
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Cover the cost of the initial exam and diagnostic testingCover costs related to tumor removal surgery beyond what is covered by the studyBring your dog to all scheduled visits at CSUFollow all study instructions and timelines
d_sv_content.whoCan: Dogs may qualify if they:Have a confirmed diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma that can be biopsiedWeigh at least 24 lbs (11 kg)Have adequate bloodworkHave not received cancer treatment within the past 2 weeksHave not received prior immunotherapyDo not have uncontrolled immune-related diseases or conditions affecting the immune systemAre able to come to CSU for all study visits
d_sv_content.benefits: Benefits:Access to an advanced, experimental cancer treatmentStudy covers up to $3,200 in study-related costsProvides $2,000 toward tumor removal surgery or other treatmentCovers cost of oral immunotherapy medications (except dispensing fees)Up to $500 coverage for treatment of study-related side effectsFinancial support available for screening testsContribute to research that may improve cancer treatment for dogsRisks:Possible side effects from immunotherapy and chemotherapyRisks related to anesthesia, biopsy, and surgeryTime commitment for multiple visitsTreatment may not be effectiveThe treatment is experimental, and its safety and effectiveness have not been fully established
d_sv_content.compensation: Study covers most treatment costs (up to $3,200), provides $2,000 toward surgery, and includes support for medications and side effect care
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: Approximately 6–8 weeks with multiple visits, including treatment day and follow-up appointments
